verdicts.reason: HELD, and I reproduced BOTH halves first-hand. CODE: §1t113s0§.as:110 'this.§1t5203s0§ = "<font color=\'#000000\'>" + §1t1521s0§.getString(175) + "</font>";' and :111 the same with '#BBBBBB' + getString(960) - verbatim. :328 'var _loc3_:Number = (param1 - 48) / (param2 - 48);' then a strict three-way: :336 'if(_loc3_ == 0)' -> :340 shows the GREY string and :342 forces visible; :344 'else if(_loc3_ > 0 && _loc3_ < 1 ...)' -> :346 'this.§1t5169s0§.visible = false;'; :348 'else if(_loc3_ >= 1)' -> :352 Snd_criticalDamage + :356 the BLACK string. strings.json["175"] = 'Critical Hit'; the table has no key '960' (2,533 entries, checked programmatically). FRAME: I opened the frame and cut exactly the crop the finding states. Under a green 20/20 bar and a blue 26/26 bar sits a THIRD bar - a uniform dark gold/brown track with NO fill segment anywhere across its width - carrying 'CANNOT CHANGE STANCE' in light-grey caps, and the yellow '150% DAMAGE' buff sits BELOW the bar stack, not in it. Every visual particular the finding asserts is there. THE FRAME AND THE CODE DO NOT DISAGREE: an empty third bar is _loc3_ == 0, which is the only branch that shows that grey label, and the same meter at >= 48 opens §1t4470s0§. OVERTURN UPHELD: SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:388 reads verbatim '| **In combat** | **Hard lock** — "CANNOT CHANGE STANCE" appears the instant a fight starts | [CONTRACT] |', and :2099 repeats it; RR:158 carries the same bold claim. A caption that the code shows and hides as a function of a live meter is an affordability message, not a lock, so the CONTRACT grade on those three lines falls. ONE THING TO LABEL: 'that label is getString(960)' is a code+frame JOIN, not a direct string lookup - 960 is absent from the Android table. The join is sound (only one branch prints a grey label, and the frame is in that branch) but it should enter the ledger as a derived identification, not as a quoted string row.

HELD on every number, and I independently settled the one thing the finding asserts without proving - that this meter is FOCUS. Verbatim: :249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;' and :250 'this.§1t4414s0§ = 0;'; :1203 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < this.§1t4415s0§)' -> :1205 '++this.§1t4414s0§;' with the HUD push at :1208 only when controlledBy == 0; :3162 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' clamped at :3163-3166; :3302 '-= this.slashUsage / 2', :3306 '-= this.slashUsage', :3310 '-= this.slashUsage * 1.5'; :3320 '+= 6' clamped to max. IDENTITY PROOF I ADDED: §1t120s0§.as:18 '§1t10128s0§:int = 1005;' and :230-231 'case §1t10128s0§: param3.§1t4414s0§ = param3.§1t4415s0§ - 1;'. skilldata.xml skill id 1005 carries <displayname>6008</displayname> and <desc>6011</desc>, and strings.json["6008"] = 'Focus', ["6011"] = 'Instantly recharges your focus bar.' The skill whose own description says it recharges the focus bar writes exactly this variable. §1t4414s0§ IS the Focus bar. Also checked and cleared a possible hole: §1t4419s0§ (param7, = baseReload = 48 + SPD*6 per §1t1523s0§.as:2274-2277) is assigned at :191 and never read on the player, so the flat +1/tick is the complete fill rule, not a partial one. OVERTURN UPHELD: RR:195 blocker (3) 'Focus numerics (max/fill/switch-cost)' names three quantities and the web payload hands over all three. The blocker falls. ONE BOUNDARY the ledger must keep: 192 is WEB-ONLY. Android MCSPlayer.as:239 sets 'this.maxreload = 5 * 24;' = 120 with a 24 threshold. The finding labels its build correctly, so this is a note, not a defect.

PRIMARY CLAIM HELD, and I closed the gap the finding left open - it never proved the mastery scale caps at 10, it only pointed at a string. Verbatim: :3262 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4421s0§ * 0.1);', :3265 '(1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1)', :3270 '_loc2_ = _loc1_ * 1.4;'. CAP PROVED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS. (i) §1t1523s0§.as:2268 passes '§1t9714s0§(1000),§1t9714s0§(1001),§1t9714s0§(1002)' as params 12/13/14; the un-obfuscated Android twin StatsManager.as:1834 passes 'getStat(1000),getStat(1001),getStat(1002)' into the same 15-slot signature whose parameters MCSPlayer.as:182 names lightMastery/balancedMastery/heavyMastery. So mastery = the player's LEVEL in skills 1000/1001/1002. (ii) skilldata.xml gives skills 1000/1001/1002 (displaynames 6000/6002/6004 = Light/Balanced/Heavy Stance Mastery) exactly ten <level><value> rows, 1..10. So m in 0..10; m=10 -> 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.4, which is RR:155's ceiling table exactly; m=9 -> 0.86 / 1.18, which is nothing. OVERTURN UPHELD BUT NARROW: what falls in RR:155 is the two characters '-9'. The sentence's substance ('these are CEILING values, not base') SURVIVES intact, and the reach half of the same sentence (300/200/100) is untouched by this function - the finding's own PARTIAL verdict and lane_impact say so, which is why I am not treating it as an inflated overturn. The RR:157 fork ('decide-and-flag the build targets mastery-9') dissolves either way. ONE SUB-CLAIM REFUTED: 'Android ... on a 0-100 mastery scale' is WRONG. Android's masteries come from the same getStat(1000/1001/1002) 10-level skills, and MCSPlayer.as:3166-3168 gates perks at 'lightMastery >= 3 / >= 4 / >= 5', identical to web §1t99s0§.as:3223-3225 - thresholds of 3/4/5 are incoherent on a 0-100 scale. Android's divergence is the COEFFICIENT (0.01 vs 0.1) and the Heavy constant (1.5 vs 1.4), not the scale, which makes Android's Light cap 0.55 and its Balanced cap 1.05. The finding's conclusion ('must not be ported') survives and is in fact stronger than it claimed.

THE CLAIM IS TRUE; THE OVERTURN IS INFLATED. First, citelint flagged QUOTE_NOT_LOCATED - that flag is a formatting artifact, not a bad cite. I located both quoted lines verbatim: :3272 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' and :3274 'return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;', with :3295-3297 zeroing the meter on the same equality. The cite RESOLVES on my own read. BUT: read RR:150-154 in context and the sentence the finding names does not fall - it is CONFIRMED. The ledger already writes 'Keep `CRIT_MULT=1.3`.' The code agrees with the ledger. Nothing there becomes false. What the evidence actually retires is (a) the parenthetical ACTION ITEM '(Read a real OG crit popup to fully seal it.)', which is an instruction, not a claim, and (b) two blockers on OTHER lines - RR:190 combat-core (2) 'crit 1.3 vs 3 final' and RR:195 skills-meters (5) 'crit proc rule (chance vs deterministic) - entirely absent'. Neither is the sentence in ledger_text. Worse for the overturn: RR:153's compounding explanation ('1.3x compounded with the per-stance crit-damage stat (Heavy x1.82) + item crit-damage') is CORROBORATED by this very code - 1.4 stance x 1.3 crit = 1.82 exactly, and §1t1243s0§ is the additive item crit-damage term, which Android names STAT_CRITICALDMG at MCSPlayer.as:3219. So the finding confirms the paragraph it claims to overturn. Real value, wrong target: promote CRIT_MULT=1.3 from wiki-authority to web-payload CONTRACT and close RR:190 (2) / RR:195 (5), but do NOT record RR:150-154 as overturned. Note also that 1.3 is web-only - Android MCSPlayer.as:3219-3221 uses 1.2 for non-Light and 1.5 for Light.

THE ARTIFACT READING HOLDS; THE OVERTURN IT ASSERTS IS WRONG. Verbatim confirmed: :3094 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4;' (Light reach, NO mastery term), :3105 '* (1 + 0.2 * this.§1t4422s0§ * 0.1)' (Balanced), :3116 '* (0.5 + 0.4 * this.§1t4423s0§ * 0.1)' with :3117-3120 'if(this.§1t4417s0§ < 100){ this.§1t4417s0§ = 100; }' (Heavy), against a damage switch at :3259-3271 that is the exact mirror. I also nailed down the stance identities the finding assumes: §1t406s0§.as:3087-3100 cycles 12220 -> 12221 printing getString(644), 12221 -> 12222 printing getString(645), 12222 -> 12220 printing getString(643), and strings.json gives 643/644/645 = 'Light Stance' / 'Balanced Stance' / 'Heavy Stance'. So 12220=Light, 12221=Balanced, 12222=Heavy, and the mapping is right. NOW THE OVERTURN. RR:156 reads 'A level-1 Shugyosha does Light x0.5 / Balanced x1.0 / Heavy x1.4 (Heavy is fixed); Heavy's *reach* also scales x0.5->x0.9.' Every clause of that is CORRECT against this code. The finding says the low endpoint is wrong because 'm=1 gives 0.54' - that conflates CHARACTER level 1 with MASTERY 1. A level-1 Shugyosha has not learned skills 1000-1002, so m=0, and at m=0 Heavy reach is exactly x0.5 while at m=10 it is exactly x0.9. The finding's own sibling in this packet (stance-damage-ceiling) concedes precisely that - 'mastery 0 gives Light 0.5 / Balanced 1.0 / Heavy 1.4 - exactly RR:156's level-1 Shugyosha row' - so the two claims contradict each other and this is the one that is wrong. The only genuine qualification to RR:156 is the 100-unit floor, which the sentence omits; an omission is not a falsification, and I do not refute for incompleteness. The finding's SECOND argument - that ceiling multipliers 1.4/1.20/0.90 are not 3:2:1, so 300/200/100 cannot be a mastery-ceiling row - is SOUND arithmetic on verified code (and I confirm it independently below), but it attacks RR:155, not the RR:156 sentence quoted in ledger_text. Keep the reach formulas; do not record RR:156 as overturned.

GATE HELD, OVERTURN HELD, BUT ONE LOAD-BEARING SENTENCE IS REFUTED. citelint said QUOTE_UNVERIFIED; I located all three quotes verbatim - :3050 'return this.§1t4469s0§() && this.§1t4414s0§ >= 48;', :249 'this.§1t4415s0§ = 8 * 24;', :3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)' - so the cite RESOLVES on my read. The cycle body at :3064-3079 steps -1->12220->12221->12222->12220 and pushes to §1t251s0§ at :3080, exactly as described. BUILD ATTRIBUTION PROVED, not assumed: §1t1523s0§.as:36 'public static var §1t9323s0§:Number = 0.717;' - this payload IS v0.717, so the overturn of RR:158's 'HARD-LOCKED in v0.717' lands on the right build. REFUTED SUB-CLAIM, and it must not reach the ledger: 'the in-combat stance switch costs no Focus and no Chi'. It costs 48 Focus. §1t99s0§.as:3160-3166 - 'if(§1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§()){ this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48; ... }' - and §1t1525s0§.as:1152-1155 defines §1t9948s0§() as 'actionState == §1t9903s0§', with §1t9903s0§ = 2 at :53, i.e. the in-battle state. So the debit fires exactly and only in combat. And the meter is not a nameless 'reload meter': §1t120s0§.as:230-231 has the skill whose own description reads 'Instantly recharges your focus bar' write §1t4414s0§ = max - 1. Correct port: in combat, require >= 48 AND spend 48 of a 192 Focus bar. Porting 'costs no Focus' ships a free switch and a wrong economy. NOTE FOR THE LEDGER: this also inverts RR:159 - see my new finding rr-159-is-inverted.

HELD, and this is the CLEANER of the two hard-lock kills in this packet - it states the rule positively and makes no cost error. new_findings.text: The Android build is a NAME KEY for the web payload's obfuscated combat variables, and using it is NOT circular. reference/decompiled/shs3_android/scripts/MCSPlayer.as:182 declares 'public function initPlayer(controlledBy:int, hp:int, maxhp:int, chi:int, maxchi:int, defense:int, baseReload:int, minDamage:int, damageRange:int, baseSlashLength:int, slashUsage:int, lightMastery:int, balancedMastery:int, heavyMastery:int, level:int)'. The web payload's §1t99s0§.as:183 declares the same 15-slot signature, and the two call sites are structurally identical - StatsManager.as:1834 'player.initPlayer(0,getPlayerStats(STAT_HP),...,getBaseReload(),getMinDamage(),getDamageRange(),getBaseSlashLength(),getSlashUsage(),getStat(1000),getStat(1001),getStat(1002),getLevel())' vs §1t1523s0§.as:2268 '...player.§1t4443s0§(0,...,§1t9588s0§(),§1t1088s0§(),§1t9591s0§(),§1t9592s0§(),§1t9594s0§(),§1t9714s0§(1000),§1t9714s0§(1001),§1t9714s0§(1002),getLevel())'. Reading §1t99s0§.as:185-199 slot by slot yields: §1t4419s0§=baseReload, §1t4420s0§=baseSlashLength, §1t4421s0§/§1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§=light/balanced/heavyMastery. The per-frame twins add §1t4414s0§=reload and §1t4415s0§=maxreload (MCSPlayer.as:1158-1160 vs §1t99s0§.as:1203-1205), §1t4417s0§=the per-stance slash length, §1t4469s0§=canChangeStance (MCSPlayer.as:2965), §1t4472s0§=nextStance (MCSPlayer.as:2975), §1t1243s0§=STAT_CRITICALDMG (MCSPlayer.as:3219). C2 forbids diffing the four data XMLs against the Android blobs because those XMLs ARE Android. This is different in kind: two independently decompiled AS3 code bundles, one obfuscated and one not. The names transfer; the NUMBERS do not, and must still be read from the web side each time.

new_findings.lane_impact: Tooling, not a ledger row: every future L0 pass on §1t99s0§.as can name its variables instead of guessing at them. This is the mechanism behind four of my seven verdicts.

new_findings.text: RR:190 combat-core blocker (1) calls the per-stance reach cap in stage px 'the one value the whole model needs' and prescribes measuring blade-FX tip-to-body span from footage. It does not need measuring. §1t1523s0§.as:2334-2348 computes it: §1t9592s0§() takes the SPD stat plus its bonus, multiplies by 1.5 under a speed buff, and returns §1t9593s0§(that), where §1t9593s0§(p) is 'var _loc2_:int = 90 + §1t7356s0§(§1t9426s0§) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(_loc2_ * param1 / (20 + param1)));'. The un-obfuscated Android twin names every term - StatsManager.as:1915-1919 'internal static function getBaseSlashLengthVal(speed:int) : int { var maxincrement:int = 90 + getPlayerStats(STAT_DAN) * 5; return int(120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * speed / (20 + speed))); }'. So BASE_SLASH_LENGTH = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5) * SPD / (20 + SPD)), a saturating curve: SPD 0 -> 120, SPD 20 -> 165, SPD -> large -> 210 at DAN 0. Reach then = base x stance, per §1t99s0§.as:3094/:3105/:3116-3120 - Light x1.4 flat, Balanced x(1 + 0.02m), Heavy x(0.5 + 0.04m) floored at 100 absolute units. THIS ALSO SETTLES THE 300/200/100 TRIPLE: at a high-SPD, DAN-0 base of ~210 the MASTERY-0 row is 294 / 210 / 105, which is the ledger's 300/200/100. The triple is a mastery-ZERO row at high SPD, not a mastery-ceiling row - the ceiling multipliers are 1.4 / 1.2 / 0.9, which cannot make 3:2:1 off any single base. That independently confirms the arithmetic objection inside claim combat-core/stance-reach-is-asymmetric (whose OTHER objection, about RR:156's low endpoint, I refuted).

new_findings.ledger_text: ① reach cap in **stage px** per stance (the one value the whole model needs; wiki gives "units" of unknown scale) — *measure blade-FX tip-to-body span in Light/Bal/Heavy from footage, or slash a dummy in a preserved build.*
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: delete blocker (1) from RR:190 and write BASE_SLASH_LENGTH = 120 + floor((90 + DAN*5)*SPD/(20+SPD)) with the three stance multipliers and the 100 floor into src/config as CONTRACT (web v0.717). Also strike '300/200/100 are MASTERY-9 CEILING values' from RR:155 - it is a mastery-0 row. What is NOT closed: the unit-to-stage-px scale factor, which still wants one frame measurement.

new_findings.text: RR:159-160 says 'The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence.' The web payload has it exactly backwards. The out-of-combat path is §1t406s0§.as:3064-3104 (the overworld portrait/stance button, MouseEvent.CLICK registered at :944): it tests for hell-zone and mail states, then cycles stance with NO meter test and NO debit, announcing getString(643/644/645) = 'Light Stance'/'Balanced Stance'/'Heavy Stance' and playing Snd_smallClick. Free. The in-combat path costs: §1t99s0§.as:3160-3166 debits 'this.§1t4414s0§ -= 48;' guarded by §1t1525s0§.§1t9948s0§(), which §1t1525s0§.as:1152-1155 defines as 'actionState == §1t9903s0§' with §1t9903s0§ = 2 at :53 - the battle state. So the resource cost exists ONLY in combat, and the recreation's Focus-gated in-combat switch is not a divergence at all: it is the original behaviour, and the thing the ledger calls real (an out-of-combat Focus cost) is the one that does not exist.
new_findings.ledger_text: The *out-of-combat* switch costing Focus IS real; the *in-combat* switch is a recreation divergence — label it, don't present it as original.
new_findings.lane_impact: L5 combat-core: strike the 'recreation divergence' label from RR:159-160 and from SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:2099. Port out-of-combat stance change as unconditional and free, and in-combat as require-48-and-spend-48 of the 192 Focus bar.

new_findings.text: A first-hand, non-circular measurement of the S0-3 build-parity hole, on the exact system this packet is about. WEB v0.717: maxreload = 8*24 = 192 (§1t99s0§.as:249), stance threshold 48 (§1t99s0§.as:3050,:3060), HUD normalisation (v-48)/(max-48) (§1t113s0§.as:328) - threshold and HUD zero-point agree, and 48/192 is exactly one quarter. ANDROID v0.682: maxreload = 5*24 = 120 (MCSPlayer.as:239), HUD normalisation (reload-24)/(maxreload-24) (MCSPlayer.as:1163-1168), and nextStance gates at 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) return;' = 20 (MCSPlayer.as:2977) - so Android's gate (20) and its HUD zero-point (24) do not even agree with each other. The web build did not merely renumber: it raised the ceiling 120 -> 192, doubled the threshold 24 -> 48, and repaired the gate/HUD mismatch. Every Focus, crit and stance-cost number therefore has to be read from the web payload; none may be ported from Android. Same conclusion from the crit branch: web is a flat *1.3 for all stances (§1t99s0§.as:3274) while Android is *1.2 for non-Light and *1.5 for Light (MCSPlayer.as:3219-3221).
new_findings.lane_impact: Discharges the S0-3 caveat's warning with a concrete example instead of a worry: combat tuning demonstrably diverges between v0.682 and v0.717 even where the data XMLs match. Any lane porting a combat number must name the build.

new_findings.text: RR:195 skills-meters blocker (5) reads 'crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) — entirely absent.' It is present and it is deterministic. §1t99s0§.as:3255-3277 is the whole damage roll: the ONLY randomness is the base roll at :3258 'var _loc1_:int = this.minDamage + Math.random() * this.damageRange;'. The crit branch at :3272 is 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ == this.§1t4415s0§)' - strict equality against maxreload, no dice - returning ':3274 return _loc2_ * 1.3 + this.§1t1243s0§;'. There is no probability term anywhere in the function. §1t4478s0§ at :3293-3297 then zeroes the meter on the same equality before applying the per-stance slash debit, so crits cannot chain: a crit costs the entire 192-point bar and the next one is 192 ticks away at the +1/tick fill rate (§1t99s0§.as:1203-1205), less whatever §1t4479s0§'s +6 refunds. The HUD says the same thing out loud - §1t113s0§.as:348-358 shows the black getString(175) = 'Critical Hit' caption and fires Snd_criticalDamage the moment the normalised bar reaches 1, i.e. the player is TOLD when the guaranteed crit is armed. §1t1243s0§ is the additive crit-damage stat (Android name STAT_CRITICALDMG, MCSPlayer.as:3219).
new_findings.ledger_text: ⑤ crit **proc** rule (chance vs deterministic) — entirely absent.
new_findings.lane_impact: L2 skills-meters: delete blocker (5) from RR:195. CRIT_PROC is deterministic - crit iff focus == FOCUS_MAX - and the crit consumes the full bar. This is the correct place to record the finding that combat-core/crit-1.3 mis-aimed at RR:150-154.

new_findings.text: Two things at once. (1) RR:195 skills-meters blocker (2) correctly denies that spacebar is slow-motion in Duels ('spacebar-slowmo belongs to the predecessor SHS2'); the positive answer is now known. §1t1541s0§.as:603-616: 'case Keyboard.SPACE:' takes the player, and 'if(!§1t10074s0§ && _loc2_.§1t4470s0§())' runs '_loc2_.§1t4472s0§();' plus Snd_smallClick, else Snd_error. SPACE cycles stance through the same 48-Focus gate as the HUD button. (2) A correction to SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:387, which grades as [CONTRACT] that out of combat stance change is an 'Instant toggle, no cooldown, no cost (SPACE or portrait click)'. Those are TWO different code paths and only one is unconditional. The portrait-click path (§1t406s0§.as:3064-3104) has no meter test at all. The SPACE path runs §1t4470s0§()/§1t4472s0§(), and §1t4472s0§ re-guards unconditionally at §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48){ return; }' - that guard is NOT wrapped in the in-battle test, unlike the -48 debit at :3160-3166. So out of combat SPACE is free but still REQUIRES 48 Focus, while the portrait click is free and unconditional. PARTIAL because I have not established §1t1541s0§'s key handler is live outside battle - it checks text-focus against BOTH §1t113s0§.instance (BattleUI) and §1t406s0§.instance (overworld) at :595-602, which suggests a global handler, but that is an inference and I am not grading it as proved.
new_findings.ledger_text: | **Out of combat** | Instant toggle, no cooldown, no cost (SPACE or portrait click) | [CONTRACT] |
new_findings.lane_impact: L8 ui-hud + L5 combat-core: bind SPACE to the stance cycle. Before re-grading SHSD_MASTER_REFERENCE.md:387, one lane needs to confirm §1t1541s0§'s SPACE handler is registered outside battle; if it is, 'Instant toggle' is wrong for the SPACE path and the [CONTRACT] grade on that cell has to split into two rows.
